name: Sirva
confidence_why: 3 independent first-hand descriptions agree (0 state the same rule, 2 refine it); none contradicts.
catalog_citation: Daniels, Don R. 2010. A preliminary phonological history of the Sogeram languages of Papua New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 49(1): 163-193. doi:10.1353/ol.0.0068.
catalog_locator: p. 168, sec. 2 'Proto-Sogeram', the paragraph directly below the PSOG inventory (1) (p. 7 in the saved Project MUSE copy); supporting remarks p. 175 sec. 4.1.2 'Vowel centering' and p. 177 sec. 4.3.1
catalog_quote: Stress is almost always word-final in the daughter languages, and it was probably also word-final in PSOG. The central vowel /ɨ/ behaves as a neutral vowel in the family, arising paragogically and epenthetically in many situations (cf. 3.1.2, 3.1.4, and 4.4.1), and being the result of any vowel-centering processes (such as 4.1.2. and 5.2.4). [p. 168] ... 4.1.2 Vowel centering (V-R > ɨ / C__C.’σopen). Unrounded vowels in closed penults centered to /ɨ/ when followed by open ultimas; the fact that PSOG probably had word-final stress helps motivate this change. [p. 175] ... While this innovation is not a bizarre phonetic development, the fact that these languages probably had word-final stress makes it a little peculiar. [p. 177]
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog has no record for Sirva; this is the first statement on stress bearing on Sirva, but it is a one-sentence family-wide generalization ('the daughter languages'), not a description of Sirva itself. Best treated as a weak family-level indication of final stress, confidence low.
new_statements.rule_in_words: A family-level remark only: stress is 'almost always word-final' in the Sogeram daughter languages (Sirva is one of them) and reconstructed as word-final for Proto-Sogeram. No language-specific stress statement for Sirva; the Sirva section (4.7, pp. 179-180) gives only the phoneme inventory and the ɨ-raising change.
new_statements.exceptions: 'almost always' - no exceptions or languages named
new_statements.identity_note: Sirva is the language Z'graggen called Sileibi (village name); Daniels 2010 p. 163 lists 'Sirva (Sileibi)' and 2020 p. 41 gives 'Sirva - language name - Sileibi - village name?'. Both works are comparative-historical works on the whole Sogeram family; the stress statements are about the family (2010) and about Mand and Manat (2020), not about a Sirva dialect.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don Roger. 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: Phonology, Lexicon, and Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. 1127 pp. Sirva: sec. 2.3.6 'Sirva Innovations' pp. 96-98; Appendix 3 'Sirva Grammar Sketch' pp. 658-765, phonology sec. 3.2-3.2.1 pp. 662-667. eScholarship qt1kj4174g.
sources.note: Nothing for Sirva: sec. 3.2 gives consonant/vowel inventories, affricate allophony, lenition, prenasalization, diphthongs, /ɨ/ phonemic status, marginal long /i/, and morphophonemics (vowel elision, coronal reduction, labial merging); no word on stress, accent or tone. Only stress remark in the whole work is p. 71 (Mand chapter): 'Further research into the stress systems of the Sogeram languages might reveal a consistent pattern.'
